	public void Map(int rows, int cols) {
		this.rows = rows;
		this.cols = cols;
		this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
		for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
			for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
				cells[r][c] = new FillableCell();
			}
		}
		Random rng = new Random();
		TerminationCell.CreateInfo sourceInfo = generateStartCellInfo();
		Coordinate sourceCoord = sourceInfo.coord;
		Direction sourceDirection = sourceInfo.direction;
		sourceCell = new TerminationCell(sourceCoord, sourceDirection);
		cells[sourceCoord.row][sourceCoord.col] = sourceCell;
		TerminationCell.CreateInfo sinkInfo = generateEndCellInfo();
		Coordinate sinkCoord = sinkInfo.coord;
		Direction sinkDirection = sinkInfo.direction;
		sinkCell = new TerminationCell(sinkCoord, sinkDirection);
		cells[sinkCoord.row][sinkCoord.col] = sinkCell;
	}

	public void Map(int rows, int cols, Cell[][] cells) {
		this.rows = rows;
		this.cols = cols;
		this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
		for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
			System.arraycopy(cells[r], 0, this.cells[r], 0, cols);
		}
		int sourceCount = 0;
		int sinkCount = 0;
		TerminationCell foundSource = null;
		TerminationCell foundSink = null;
		for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
			for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
				Cell cell = this.cells[r][c];
				if (cell instanceof TerminationCell) {
					TerminationCell termCell = (TerminationCell) cell;
					if (termCell.isSource()) {
						sourceCount++;
						foundSource = termCell;
					} else if (termCell.isSink()) {
						sinkCount++;
						foundSink = termCell;
					}
				}
			}
		}
		if (sourceCount != 1 || foundSource == null) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must contain exactly one source cell.");
		}
		int srcRow = foundSource.coord.row;
		int srcCol = foundSource.coord.col;
		if (srcRow == 0 || srcRow == rows - 1 || srcCol == 0 || srcCol == cols - 1) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source cell must not be on the edge.");
		}
		Cell sourceAdjacent = cells[srcRow + foundSource.direction.getOffset().row][srcCol
				+ foundSource.direction.getOffset().col];
		if (sourceAdjacent instanceof Wall) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source cell must not point into a wall.");
		}
		if (sinkCount != 1 || foundSink == null) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must contain exactly one sink cell.");
		}
		int sinkRow = foundSink.coord.row;
		int sinkCol = foundSink.coord.col;
		if (!(sinkRow == 0 || sinkRow == rows - 1 || sinkCol == 0 || sinkCol == cols - 1)) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink cell must be on the edge.");
		}
		Coordinate sinkAdjacentCoord = sinkRow + foundSink.direction.getOffset().row.sinkCol
				+ foundSink.direction.getOffset().col;
		if (sinkAdjacentCoord.row >= 0 && sinkAdjacentCoord.row < rows && sinkAdjacentCoord.col >= 0
				&& sinkAdjacentCoord.col < cols) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink cell must point outside the map.");
		}
		this.sourceCell = foundSource;
		this.sinkCell = foundSink;
	}

	boolean tryPlacePipe(int row, int col, Pipe p) {
		int r = row - 1;
		int c = col - 1;
		if (r < 0 || r >= rows || c < 0 || c >= cols) {
			return false;
		}
		Cell targetCell = cells[r][c];
		if (!(targetCell instanceof FillableCell)) {
			return false;
		}
		FillableCell fillable = (FillableCell) targetCell;
		if (fillable.hasPipe()) {
			return false;
		}
		fillable.setPipe(p);
		return true;
	}

	public void undo(final Coordinate coord) {
		int row = coord.row;
		int col = coord.col;
		if (row < 0 || row >= rows || col < 0 || col >= cols) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Coordinate is out of bounds.");
		}
		Cell cell = cells[row][col];
		if (!(cell instanceof FillableCell)) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cell at the coordinate is not fillable.");
		}
		cells[row][col] = new FillableCell();
		filledTiles.remove(coord);
	}

	public void fillTiles(int distance) {
		if (sourceCell == null || cells == null) {
			return;
		}
		Queue<Coordinate> queue = new LinkedList<>();
		Map<Coordinate, Integer> visitedDistances = new HashMap<>();
		Coordinate start = sourceCell.coord;
		queue.offer(start);
		visitedDistances.put(start, 0);
		filledTiles.add(start);
		cells[start.row][start.col].setFilled();
		while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
			Coordinate current = queue.poll();
			int currentDist = visitedDistances.get(current);
			if (currentDist >= distance) {
				continue;
			}
			for (Direction dir : Direction.values()) {
				int newRow = current.row + dir.getOffset().row;
				int newCol = current.col + dir.getOffset().col;
				if (newRow < 0 || newRow >= rows || newCol < 0 || newCol >= cols) {
					continue;
				}
				Coordinate neighbor = new Coordinate(newRow, newCol);
				if (visitedDistances.containsKey(neighbor)) {
					continue;
				}
				Cell neighborCell = cells[newRow][newCol];
				if (neighborCell instanceof FillableCell) {
					neighborCell.setFilled();
					filledTiles.add(neighbor);
					visitedDistances.put(neighbor, currentDist + 1);
					queue.offer(neighbor);
				}
			}
		}
	}

	public boolean checkPath() {
		if (sourceCell == null || sinkCell == null) {
			return false;
		}
		Set<Coordinate> visited = new HashSet<>();
		Queue<Coordinate> queue = new LinkedList<>();
		queue.offer(sourceCell.coord);
		visited.add(sourceCell.coord);
		while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
			Coordinate current = queue.poll();
			if (current.equals(sinkCell.coord)) {
				return true;
			}
			Cell currentCell = cells[current.row][current.col];
			List<Direction> outgoingDirections = new ArrayList<>();
			if (currentCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
				TerminationCell termCell = (TerminationCell) currentCell;
				outgoingDirections.add(termCell.direction);
			} else if (currentCell instanceof Pipe) {
				Pipe pipe = (Pipe) currentCell;
				outgoingDirections.addAll(pipe.getOpenDirections());
			} else {
				continue;
			}
			for (Direction dir : outgoingDirections) {
				int newRow = current.row + dir.getOffset().row;
				int newCol = current.col + dir.getOffset().col;
				if (newRow < 0 || newRow >= rows || newCol < 0 || newCol >= cols) {
					continue;
				}
				Coordinate neighborCoord = new Coordinate(newRow, newCol);
				if (visited.contains(neighborCoord)) {
					continue;
				}
				Cell neighborCell = cells[newRow][newCol];
				if (neighborCell instanceof FillableCell || neighborCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
					boolean connectsBack = false;
					if (neighborCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
						connectsBack = true;
					} else if (neighborCell instanceof Pipe) {
						Pipe neighborPipe = (Pipe) neighborCell;
						Direction oppositeDir = dir.getOpposite();
						if (neighborPipe.getOpenDirections().contains(oppositeDir)) {
							connectsBack = true;
						}
					}
					if (connectsBack) {
						visited.add(neighborCoord);
						queue.offer(neighborCoord);
					}
				}
			}
		}
		return false;
	}
}

Response Text:---
The errors indicate that the `Map` class does not have constructors accepting `(int, int)` or `(int, int, Cell[][])` parameters, yet the tests and code are attempting to instantiate `Map` with these constructors. To fix this, you should define a constructor in the `Map` class that accepts `(int rows, int cols)` and initializes the `cells` array accordingly, along with setting the source and sink cells.

Here's a correct implementation of the `Map` class with the necessary constructor:

```java
package game.map;

import game.map.cells.Cell;
import game.map.cells.FillableCell;
import game.map.cells.TerminationCell;
import game.pipes.Pipe;
import io.Deserializer;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import util.Coordinate;
import util.Direction;
import util.StringUtils;

import java.util.*;

/**
 * Map of the game.
 */
public class Map {
    private final int rows;
    private final int cols;
    @NotNull
    final Cell[][] cells;

    private TerminationCell sourceCell;
    private TerminationCell sinkCell;

    @NotNull
    private final Set<Coordinate> filledTiles = new HashSet<>();
    private int prevFilledTiles = 0;
    private Integer prevFilledDistance;

    /**
     * Constructor to initialize the map with given rows and columns.
     */
    public Map(int rows, int cols) {
        this.rows = rows;
        this.cols = cols;
        this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
        for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
            for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
                cells[r][c] = new FillableCell();
            }
        }
        // Initialize source and sink cells
        Random rng = new Random();
        TerminationCell.CreateInfo sourceInfo = generateStartCellInfo();
        Coordinate sourceCoord = sourceInfo.coord;
        Direction sourceDirection = sourceInfo.direction;
        sourceCell = new TerminationCell(sourceCoord, sourceDirection);
        cells[sourceCoord.row][sourceCoord.col] = sourceCell;
        TerminationCell.CreateInfo sinkInfo = generateEndCellInfo();
        Coordinate sinkCoord = sinkInfo.coord;
        Direction sinkDirection = sinkInfo.direction;
        sinkCell = new TerminationCell(sinkCoord, sinkDirection);
        cells[sinkCoord.row][sinkCoord.col] = sinkCell;
    }

    // Existing methods...
}
```

**Explanation:**  
- This constructor creates a new map with specified dimensions.  
- It initializes all cells as `FillableCell`.  
- It generates and sets the source and sink cells at appropriate positions.  
- This aligns with the usage in your tests and code, resolving the compilation errors.

Response Text:---
The `getConnections()` method should return an array of `Direction` enums indicating the directions in which the pipe connects, based on its shape. Typically, a pipe's connections depend on its shape: for example, a horizontal pipe connects left and right, a vertical pipe connects up and down, and a cross connects all four directions.

Here's a complete implementation for the method:

```java
public Direction[] getConnections() {
    if (shape == null) {
        throw new IllegalStateException("Pipe shape is not initialized");
    }
    switch (shape) {
        case HORIZONTAL:
            return new Direction[] { Direction.LEFT, Direction.RIGHT };
        case VERTICAL:
            return new Direction[] { Direction.UP, Direction.DOWN };
        case TOP_LEFT:
            return new Direction[] { Direction.UP, Direction.LEFT };
        case TOP_RIGHT:
            return new Direction[] { Direction.UP, Direction.RIGHT };
        case BOTTOM_LEFT:
            return new Direction[] { Direction.DOWN, Direction.LEFT };
        case BOTTOM_RIGHT:
            return new Direction[] { Direction.DOWN, Direction.RIGHT };
        case CROSS:
            return new Direction[] { Direction.UP, Direction.DOWN, Direction.LEFT, Direction.RIGHT };
        default:
            throw new IllegalStateException("Unknown pipe shape: " + shape);
    }
}
```

This implementation checks the shape of the pipe and returns the corresponding directions. If the shape is null, it throws an `IllegalStateException` as specified.

6. Check for a winner using `getWinner()`.
7. Continue until a winner is found.

Here's a complete implementation of the `start()` method:

```java
@Override
public Player start() {
    // reset all things
    Player winner = null;
    this.numMoves = 0;
    this.board = configuration.getInitialBoard();
    this.currentPlayer = null;
    this.refreshOutput();

    // Get the list of players in order
    ArrayList<Player> players = new ArrayList<>(configuration.getPlayers());
    int playerIndex = 0;

    while (true) {
        // Determine current player based on order
        currentPlayer = players.get(playerIndex);
        // Get available moves for current player
        Move[] availableMoves = getAvailableMoves(currentPlayer);
        // Retrieve next move from player
        Move move = currentPlayer.nextMove(this, availableMoves);
        // Make the move
        movePiece(move);
        // Refresh output after move
        this.refreshOutput();
        // Update move count
        this.numMoves++;
        // Get the piece moved (assuming move has source and destination)
        Piece movedPiece = board[move.source().x()][move.source().y()];
        // Update score for current player
        updateScore(currentPlayer, movedPiece, move);
        // Check for winner
        winner = getWinner(currentPlayer, movedPiece, move);
        if (winner != null) {
            System.out.println();
            System.out.println("Congratulations! ");
            System.out.printf("Winner: %s%s%s\n", winner.getColor(), winner.getName(), Color.DEFAULT);
            return winner;
        }
        // Move to next player
        playerIndex = (playerIndex + 1) % players.size();
    }
}
```

**Explanation:**

- The method initializes the game state.
- It retrieves the list of players and cycles through them in order.
- For each turn:
  - It gets the current player.
  - Retrieves all valid moves for that player.
  - Asks the player for their next move.
  - Executes the move with `movePiece()`.
  - Refreshes the game display.
  - Updates the player's score.
  - Checks if the move resulted in a win.
- The loop continues until a winner is found, at which point it announces and returns the winner.

This implementation ensures the game proceeds turn-by-turn, respecting the order of players, and correctly terminates when a winner emerges.

The `getWinner` method should determine if the last move resulted in a player winning the game. Typically, in such games, a player wins when they meet certain conditions, such as controlling all opponent pieces, reaching a specific position, or achieving a particular pattern. Since the exact game rules are not provided, a common approach is to check if the opponent has any remaining pieces or if the last move fulfills a winning condition.

Assuming the game involves eliminating opponent pieces or reaching a goal, a typical implementation might:

- Check if the opponent has any remaining pieces on the board.
- If not, the last player who made a move is the winner.
- Otherwise, return null indicating the game continues.

Here's a plausible implementation based on common game logic:

```java
@Override
public Player getWinner(Player lastPlayer, Piece lastPiece, Move lastMove) {
    // Determine the opponent player
    Player opponent = null;
    for (Player p : configuration.getPlayers()) {
        if (!p.equals(lastPlayer)) {
            opponent = p;
            break;
        }
    }
    if (opponent == null) {
        return null; // No opponent found, game might be incomplete
    }

    // Check if opponent has any remaining pieces on the board
    boolean opponentHasPieces = false;
    for (int x = 0; x < board.length; x++) {
        for (int y = 0; y < board[x].length; y++) {
            Piece piece = board[x][y];
            if (piece != null && piece.getOwner().equals(opponent)) {
                opponentHasPieces = true;
                break;
            }
        }
        if (opponentHasPieces) {
            break;
        }
    }

    // If opponent has no pieces left, lastPlayer wins
    if (!opponentHasPieces) {
        return lastPlayer;
    }

    // No winner yet
    return null;
}
```

**Note:** Adjust the logic based on the actual game rules if they specify different winning conditions.

The `updateScore` method calculates the Manhattan distance between the move's source and destination places and adds this value to the player's current score. This approach aligns with the description that each move's score is based on the Manhattan distance traveled.

Here's the complete implementation of the `updateScore` method:

```java
public void updateScore(Player player, Piece piece, Move move) {
    Place source = move.source();
    Place destination = move.destination();
    int distance = Math.abs(source.x() - destination.x()) + Math.abs(source.y() - destination.y());
    int currentScore = player.getScore();
    player.setScore(currentScore + distance);
}

The method `getAvailableMoves(Player player)` needs to iterate over all pieces belonging to the given player on the board, retrieve each piece's available moves via `Piece#getAvailableMoves(Game, Place)`, and collect all valid moves into a list, ensuring no invalid moves are included. Since `Piece#getAvailableMoves` may return moves that are not valid in the current game state, we should validate each move before adding it to the result.

Here's a complete implementation:

```java
public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Player player) {
    ArrayList<Move> validMoves = new ArrayList<>();
    for (int x = 0; x < board.length; x++) {
        for (int y = 0; y < board[x].length; y++) {
            Piece piece = board[x][y];
            if (piece != null && piece.getOwner().equals(player)) {
                Place currentPlace = new Place(x, y);
                for (Move move : piece.getAvailableMoves(this, currentPlace)) {
                    // Validate move: ensure move destination is within board bounds and not blocked
                    Place dest = move.destination();
                    int dx = dest.x();
                    int dy = dest.y();
                    if (dx >= 0 && dx < board.length && dy >= 0 && dy < board[0].length) {
                        Piece targetPiece = board[dx][dy];
                        // Check if destination is empty or occupied by opponent
                        if (targetPiece == null || !targetPiece.getOwner().equals(player)) {
                            // Additional validation can be added here if needed
                            validMoves.add(move);
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    return validMoves.toArray(new Move[0]);
}
```

- Iterate over each cell in the `board`.
- Check if the cell contains a piece owned by the specified `player`.
- For each such piece, retrieve its available moves.
- Validate each move by checking if the destination is within bounds and not occupied by the player's own piece.
- Collect all valid moves into a list and return as an array.

This implementation ensures all returned moves are valid within the current game state.

package assignment;

public class JesonMor extends Game {
	public JesonMor(Configuration configuration) {
		super(configuration);
	}

	/**
	 * Get all available moves of one player.
	 * This method is called when it is the {@link Player}'s turn to make a move.
	 * It will iterate all {@link Piece}s belonging to the {@link Player} on board and obtain available moves of
	 * each of the {@link Piece}s through method {@link Piece#getAvailableMoves(Game, Place)} of each {@link Piece}.
	 * <p>
	 * <strong>Attention: Student should make sure all {@link Move}s returned are valid.</strong>
	 *
	 * @param player the player whose available moves to get
	 * @return an array of available moves
	 */
	public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Player player) {
		// TODO student implementation
		return new Move[0];
	}

	@Override
	public Player start() {
		Player winner = null;
		this.numMoves = 0;
		this.board = configuration.getInitialBoard();
		this.currentPlayer = null;
		this.refreshOutput();
		ArrayList<Player> players = new ArrayList<>(configuration.getPlayers());
		int playerIndex = 0;
		while (true) {
			currentPlayer = players.get(playerIndex);
			Move[] availableMoves = getAvailableMoves(currentPlayer);
			Move move = currentPlayer.nextMove(this, availableMoves);
			movePiece(move);
			this.refreshOutput();
			this.numMoves++;
			Piece movedPiece = board[move.source().x()][move.source().y()];
			updateScore(currentPlayer, movedPiece, move);
			winner = getWinner(currentPlayer, movedPiece, move);
			if (winner != null) {
				System.out.println();
				System.out.println("Congratulations! ");
				System.out.printf("Winner: %s%s%s\n", winner.getColor(), winner.getName(), Color.DEFAULT);
				return winner;
			}
			playerIndex = (playerIndex + 1) % players.size();
		}
	}

	@Override
	public Player getWinner(Player lastPlayer, Piece lastPiece, Move lastMove) {
		Player opponent = null;
		for (Player p : configuration.getPlayers()) {
			if (!p.equals(lastPlayer)) {
				opponent = p;
				break;
			}
		}
		if (opponent == null) {
			return null;
		}
		boolean opponentHasPieces = false;
		for (int x = 0; x < board.length; x++) {
			for (int y = 0; y < board[x].length; y++) {
				Piece piece = board[x][y];
				if (piece != null && piece.getOwner().equals(opponent)) {
					opponentHasPieces = true;
					break;
				}
			}
			if (opponentHasPieces) {
				break;
			}
		}
		if (!opponentHasPieces) {
			return lastPlayer;
		}
		return null;
	}

	public void updateScore(Player player, Piece piece, Move move) {
		Place source = move.source();
		Place destination = move.destination();
		int distance = Math.abs(source.x() - destination.x()) + Math.abs(source.y() - destination.y());
		int currentScore = player.getScore();
		player.setScore(currentScore + distance);
	}

	public void movePiece(Move move) {
		Place source = move.source();
		Place destination = move.destination();
		Piece movingPiece = board[source.x()][source.y()];
		board[destination.x()][destination.y()] = movingPiece;
		board[source.x()][source.y()] = null;
	}
}

public class JesonMor extends Game {
	public JesonMor(Configuration configuration) {
		super(configuration);
	}

	/**
	 * Get all available moves of one player.
	 * This method is called when it is the {@link Player}'s turn to make a move.
	 * It will iterate all {@link Piece}s belonging to the {@link Player} on board and obtain available moves of
	 * each of the {@link Piece}s through method {@link Piece#getAvailableMoves(Game, Place)} of each {@link Piece}.
	 * <p>
	 * <strong>Attention: Student should make sure all {@link Move}s returned are valid.</strong>
	 *
	 * @param player the player whose available moves to get
	 * @return an array of available moves
	 */
	public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Player player) {
		// TODO student implementation
		return new Move[0];
	}

	@Override
	public Player start() {
		Player winner = null;
		this.numMoves = 0;
		this.board = configuration.getInitialBoard();
		this.currentPlayer = null;
		this.refreshOutput();
		ArrayList<Player> players = new ArrayList<>(configuration.getPlayers());
		int playerIndex = 0;
		while (true) {
			currentPlayer = players.get(playerIndex);
			Move[] availableMoves = getAvailableMoves(currentPlayer);
			Move move = currentPlayer.nextMove(this, availableMoves);
			movePiece(move);
			this.refreshOutput();
			this.numMoves++;
			Piece movedPiece = board[move.source().x()][move.source().y()];
			updateScore(currentPlayer, movedPiece, move);
			winner = getWinner(currentPlayer, movedPiece, move);
			if (winner != null) {
				System.out.println();
				System.out.println("Congratulations! ");
				System.out.printf("Winner: %s%s%s\n", winner.getColor(), winner.getName(), Color.DEFAULT);
				return winner;
			}
			playerIndex = (playerIndex + 1) % players.size();
		}
	}

	@Override
	public Player getWinner(Player lastPlayer, Piece lastPiece, Move lastMove) {
		Player opponent = null;
		for (Player p : configuration.getPlayers()) {
			if (!p.equals(lastPlayer)) {
				opponent = p;
				break;
			}
		}
		if (opponent == null) {
			return null;
		}
		boolean opponentHasPieces = false;
		for (int x = 0; x < board.length; x++) {
			for (int y = 0; y < board[x].length; y++) {
				Piece piece = board[x][y];
				if (piece != null && piece.getOwner().equals(opponent)) {
					opponentHasPieces = true;
					break;
				}
			}
			if (opponentHasPieces) {
				break;
			}
		}
		if (!opponentHasPieces) {
			return lastPlayer;
		}
		return null;
	}

	public void updateScore(Player player, Piece piece, Move move) {
		Place source = move.source();
		Place destination = move.destination();
		int distance = Math.abs(source.x() - destination.x()) + Math.abs(source.y() - destination.y());
		int currentScore = player.getScore();
		player.setScore(currentScore + distance);
	}

	public void movePiece(Move move) {
		Place source = move.source();
		Place destination = move.destination();
		Piece movingPiece = board[source.x()][source.y()];
		board[destination.x()][destination.y()] = movingPiece;
		board[source.x()][source.y()] = null;
	}
}

- BOT: 
public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Player player) {
    ArrayList<Move> validMoves = new ArrayList<>();
    for (int x = 0; x < board.length; x++) {
        for (int y = 0; y < board[x].length; y++) {
            Piece piece = board[x][y];
            if (piece != null && piece.getOwner().equals(player)) {
                Place currentPlace = new Place(x, y);
                for (Move move : piece.getAvailableMoves(this, currentPlace)) {
                    // Validate move: ensure move destination is within board bounds and not blocked
                    Place dest = move.destination();
                    int dx = dest.x();
                    int dy = dest.y();
                    if (dx >= 0 && dx < board.length && dy >= 0 && dy < board[0].length) {
                        Piece targetPiece = board[dx][dy];
                        // Check if destination is empty or occupied by opponent
                        if (targetPiece == null || !targetPiece.getOwner().equals(player)) {
                            // Additional validation can be added here if needed
                            validMoves.add(move);
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    return validMoves.toArray(new Move[0]);
}

public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Player player) {
    ArrayList<Move> validMoves = new ArrayList<>();
    for (int x = 0; x < board.length; x++) {
        for (int y = 0; y < board[x].length; y++) {
            Piece piece = board[x][y];
            if (piece != null && piece.getPlayer().equals(player)) {
                Place currentPlace = new Place(x, y);
                for (Move move : piece.getAvailableMoves(this, currentPlace)) {
                    Place dest = move.getDestination();
                    int dx = dest.x();
                    int dy = dest.y();
                    if (dx >= 0 && dx < board.length && dy >= 0 && dy < board[0].length) {
                        Piece targetPiece = board[dx][dy];
                        if (targetPiece == null || !targetPiece.getPlayer().equals(player)) {
                            validMoves.add(move);
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    return validMoves.toArray(new Move[0]);
}

public class JesonMor extends Game {
	public JesonMor(Configuration configuration) {
		super(configuration);
	}

	/**
	 * Get all available moves of one player.
	 * This method is called when it is the {@link Player}'s turn to make a move.
	 * It will iterate all {@link Piece}s belonging to the {@link Player} on board and obtain available moves of
	 * each of the {@link Piece}s through method {@link Piece#getAvailableMoves(Game, Place)} of each {@link Piece}.
	 * <p>
	 * <strong>Attention: Student should make sure all {@link Move}s returned are valid.</strong>
	 *
	 * @param player the player whose available moves to get
	 * @return an array of available moves
	 */
	public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Player player) {
		// TODO student implementation
		return new Move[0];
	}

	@Override
	public Player start() {
		Player winner = null;
		this.numMoves = 0;
		this.board = configuration.getInitialBoard();
		this.currentPlayer = null;
		this.refreshOutput();
		ArrayList<Player> players = new ArrayList<>(configuration.getPlayers());
		int playerIndex = 0;
		while (true) {
			currentPlayer = players.get(playerIndex);
			Move[] availableMoves = getAvailableMoves(currentPlayer);
			Move move = currentPlayer.nextMove(this, availableMoves);
			movePiece(move);
			this.refreshOutput();
			this.numMoves++;
			Piece movedPiece = board[move.source().x()][move.source().y()];
			updateScore(currentPlayer, movedPiece, move);
			winner = getWinner(currentPlayer, movedPiece, move);
			if (winner != null) {
				System.out.println();
				System.out.println("Congratulations! ");
				System.out.printf("Winner: %s%s%s\n", winner.getColor(), winner.getName(), Color.DEFAULT);
				return winner;
			}
			playerIndex = (playerIndex + 1) % players.size();
		}
	}

	@Override
	public Player getWinner(Player lastPlayer, Piece lastPiece, Move lastMove) {
		Player opponent = null;
		for (Player p : configuration.getPlayers()) {
			if (!p.equals(lastPlayer)) {
				opponent = p;
				break;
			}
		}
		if (opponent == null) {
			return null;
		}
		boolean opponentHasPieces = false;
		for (int x = 0; x < board.length; x++) {
			for (int y = 0; y < board[x].length; y++) {
				Piece piece = board[x][y];
				if (piece != null && piece.getOwner().equals(opponent)) {
					opponentHasPieces = true;
					break;
				}
			}
			if (opponentHasPieces) {
				break;
			}
		}
		if (!opponentHasPieces) {
			return lastPlayer;
		}
		return null;
	}

	public void updateScore(Player player, Piece piece, Move move) {
		Place source = move.source();
		Place destination = move.destination();
		int distance = Math.abs(source.x() - destination.x()) + Math.abs(source.y() - destination.y());
		int currentScore = player.getScore();
		player.setScore(currentScore + distance);
	}

	public void movePiece(Move move) {
		Place source = move.source();
		Place destination = move.destination();
		Piece movingPiece = board[source.x()][source.y()];
		board[destination.x()][destination.y()] = movingPiece;
		board[source.x()][source.y()] = null;
	}
}

- BOT: 
public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Player player) {
    ArrayList<Move> validMoves = new ArrayList<>();
    for (int x = 0; x < board.length; x++) {
        for (int y = 0; y < board[x].length; y++) {
            Piece piece = board[x][y];
            if (piece != null && piece.getOwner().equals(player)) {
                Place currentPlace = new Place(x, y);
                for (Move move : piece.getAvailableMoves(this, currentPlace)) {
                    // Validate move: ensure move destination is within board bounds and not blocked
                    Place dest = move.destination();
                    int dx = dest.x();
                    int dy = dest.y();
                    if (dx >= 0 && dx < board.length && dy >= 0 && dy < board[0].length) {
                        Piece targetPiece = board[dx][dy];
                        // Check if destination is empty or occupied by opponent
                        if (targetPiece == null || !targetPiece.getOwner().equals(player)) {
                            // Additional validation can be added here if needed
                            validMoves.add(move);
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    return validMoves.toArray(new Move[0]);
}

public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Player player) {
    ArrayList<Move> validMoves = new ArrayList<>();
    for (int x = 0; x < board.length; x++) {
        for (int y = 0; y < board[x].length; y++) {
            Piece piece = board[x][y];
            if (piece != null && piece.getPlayer().equals(player)) {
                Place currentPlace = new Place(x, y);
                for (Move move : piece.getAvailableMoves(this, currentPlace)) {
                    Place dest = move.getDestination();
                    int dx = dest.x();
                    int dy = dest.y();
                    if (dx >= 0 && dx < board.length && dy >= 0 && dy < board[0].length) {
                        Piece targetPiece = board[dx][dy];
                        if (targetPiece == null || !targetPiece.getPlayer().equals(player)) {
                            validMoves.add(move);
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    return validMoves.toArray(new Move[0]);
}

1. The method `getOwner()` does not exist in the `Piece` class; instead, it should be `getPlayer()`.
2. The method `destination()` (and similarly `source()`) does not exist in the `Move` class; instead, use `getDestination()` and `getSource()`.

```java
public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Player player) {
    ArrayList<Move> validMoves = new ArrayList<Move>();
    for (int x = 0; x < board.length; x++) {
        for (int y = 0; y < board[x].length; y++) {
            Piece piece = board[x][y];
            if (piece != null && piece.getPlayer().equals(player)) {
                Place currentPlace = new Place(x, y);
                for (Move move : piece.getAvailableMoves(this, currentPlace)) {
                    Place dest = move.getDestination();
                    int dx = dest.x();
                    int dy = dest.y();
                    if (dx >= 0 && dx < board.length && dy >= 0 && dy < board[0].length) {
                        Piece targetPiece = board[dx][dy];
                        if (targetPiece == null || !targetPiece.getPlayer().equals(player)) {
                            validMoves.add(move);
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    return validMoves.toArray(new Move[0]);
}

```java
public static Game createGame(int size, int numMovesProtection) {
    // Create the user player and the computer player
    ConsolePlayer userPlayer = new ConsolePlayer("UserPlayer");
    RandomPlayer computerPlayer = new RandomPlayer("ComputerPlayer");
    
    // Initialize configuration with user player first to ensure they move first
    Player[] players = new Player[] { userPlayer, computerPlayer };
    Configuration configuration = new Configuration(size, players, numMovesProtection);
    
    // Add initial pieces to the gameboard
    // For example, place a Knight for the user at (0,0)
    Knight userKnight = new Knight(userPlayer);
    configuration.addInitialPiece(userKnight, 0, 0);
    
    // Place a Knight for the computer at (size - 1, size - 1) (opposite corner)
    Knight computerKnight = new Knight(computerPlayer);
    configuration.addInitialPiece(computerKnight, size - 1, size - 1);
    
    // Additional initial pieces can be added here as needed
    
    // Create and return the game object
    return new JesonMor(configuration);
}
```

	 * Create and initialize a game.
	 * Student should first construct a {@link Configuration} object with two players.

	 * @param numMovesProtection number of moves with capture protection
	 * @return the game object
	 */
	public static Game createGame(int size, int numMovesProtection) {
		// TODO student implementation
		// The following lines are example of constructing a game object, you may modify them as you wish.
		ConsolePlayer userPlayer = new ConsolePlayer("UserPlayer");
		RandomPlayer computerPlayer = new RandomPlayer("ComputerPlayer");
		// we give
		Configuration configuration = new Configuration(size, new Player[] { userPlayer, computerPlayer },
				numMovesProtection);
		Knight knight1 = new Knight(userPlayer);
		Knight knight2 = new Knight(computerPlayer);
		// put knight1 at place(0,0) on the gameboard
		configuration.addInitialPiece(knight1, 0, 0);
		// put knight2 at place(1,0) on the gameboard
		configuration.addInitialPiece(knight2, 1, 0);
		return new JesonMor(configuration);
	}

Response Text:---
The method `getAvailableMoves` should generate all possible knight moves based on the current position (`source`) on the game board, filter out invalid moves (e.g., moves outside the board or blocked), and return the valid ones. 

A knight moves in an "L" shape: two steps in one direction and one step perpendicular to that. The relative move offsets are well-known: (±2, ±1) and (±1, ±2).

Here's a complete implementation:

```java
@Override
public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Game game, Place source) {
    int[][] moveOffsets = {
        {2, 1}, {2, -1}, {-2, 1}, {-2, -1},
        {1, 2}, {1, -2}, {-1, 2}, {-1, -2}
    };
    ArrayList<Move> validMoves = new ArrayList<>();
    int currentRow = source.getRow();
    int currentCol = source.getCol();

    for (int[] offset : moveOffsets) {
        int newRow = currentRow + offset[0];
        int newCol = currentCol + offset[1];
        Place targetPlace = new Place(newRow, newCol);
        Move move = new Move(source, targetPlace);
        if (validateMove(game, move)) {
            validMoves.add(move);
        }
    }

    return validMoves.toArray(new Move[0]);
}
```

**Explanation:**
- Defines all 8 possible knight moves.
- Iterates over each move, computes the target position.
- Creates a `Move` object from the source to the target.
- Uses `validateMove` to ensure the move is within bounds and not blocked.
- Collects all valid moves into a list and returns them as an array.

This implementation ensures all valid moves are considered and filtered according to the game's rules.

		return new Move[0];
	}

	private boolean validateMove(Game game, Move move) {
		var rules = new Rule[] { new OutOfBoundaryRule(), new OccupiedRule(), new VacantRule(), new NilMoveRule(),
				new FirstNMovesProtectionRule(game.getConfiguration().getNumMovesProtection()), new KnightMoveRule(),
				new KnightBlockRule(), };
		for (var rule : rules) {
			if (!rule.validate(game, move)) {
				return false;
			}
		}
		return true;
	}

Response Text:---
The task is to implement the `getAvailableMoves` method for the `Archer` class, which moves similarly to the cannon in Xiangqi. The Archer can move any number of empty squares along a rank or file, but to capture, it must jump over exactly one piece (the "screen") and land on an opponent's piece.

**Approach:**
- For each of the four directions (up, down, left, right):
  - Traverse squares until hitting the boundary or an occupied square.
  - First, move through empty squares, adding each as a valid move.
  - If an occupied square is encountered, check if the next occupied square in the same direction contains an opponent's piece:
    - If yes, add that move as a capture move.
- Use the `validateMove` method to ensure each move is valid before adding.

Here's the complete implementation:

```java
@Override
public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Game game, Place source) {
    ArrayList<Move> moves = new ArrayList<>();
    int[][] directions = { {1, 0}, {-1, 0}, {0, 1}, {0, -1} }; // down, up, right, left
    int maxRow = game.getBoard().getNumRows();
    int maxCol = game.getBoard().getNumCols();

    for (int[] dir : directions) {
        int row = source.getRow();
        int col = source.getCol();
        boolean screenFound = false;

        while (true) {
            row += dir[0];
            col += dir[1];

            // Check boundary
            if (row < 0 || row >= maxRow || col < 0 || col >= maxCol) {
                break;
            }

            Place targetPlace = new Place(row, col);
            Move move = new Move(source, targetPlace);

            if (!validateMove(game, move)) {
                // Move is invalid, skip
                continue;
            }

            // Check occupancy
            Piece pieceAtTarget = game.getBoard().getPieceAt(targetPlace);
            if (pieceAtTarget == null) {
                // Empty square
                if (!screenFound) {
                    // Can move freely if no screen has been found yet
                    moves.add(move);
                } else {
                    // Can't land on empty after a screen
                    // continue searching
                }
            } else {
                // Occupied square
                if (!screenFound) {
                    // First obstacle: mark screen found and continue
                    screenFound = true;
                } else {
                    // Second obstacle: check if opponent's piece
                    if (pieceAtTarget.getPlayer() != this.getPlayer()) {
                        // Capture move
                        moves.add(move);
                    }
                    // After encountering second obstacle, stop in this direction
                    break;
                }
            }
        }
    }

    return moves.toArray(new Move[0]);
}
```

**Explanation:**
- Iterates over four directions.
- Moves step-by-step, adding empty squares as valid moves until hitting an obstacle.
- When encountering the first obstacle (screen), continues searching.
- When encountering the second obstacle, if it's an opponent's piece, adds a capture move.
- Uses `validateMove` to ensure each move adheres to game rules.

This implementation ensures all valid moves for the Archer are considered, respecting the movement rules similar to a Xiangqi cannon.

	private boolean validateMove(Game game, Move move) {
		var rules = new Rule[] { new OutOfBoundaryRule(), new OccupiedRule(), new VacantRule(), new NilMoveRule(),
				new FirstNMovesProtectionRule(game.getConfiguration().getNumMovesProtection()), new ArcherMoveRule(), };
		for (var rule : rules) {
			if (!rule.validate(game, move)) {
				return false;
			}
		}
		return true;
	}
}

```java
@Override
public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Game game, Place source) {
    ArrayList<Move> moves = new ArrayList<>();
    int[][] directions = { {1, 0}, {-1, 0}, {0, 1}, {0, -1} }; // down, up, right, left
    int maxRow = game.getBoard().getNumRows();
    int maxCol = game.getBoard().getNumCols();

    for (int[] dir : directions) {
        int row = source.row; // or source.getRow() if method exists
        int col = source.col; // or source.getCol() if method exists
        boolean screenFound = false;

        while (true) {
            row += dir[0];
            col += dir[1];

            // Check boundary
            if (row < 0 || row >= maxRow || col < 0 || col >= maxCol) {
                break;
            }

            Place targetPlace = new Place(row, col);
            Move move = new Move(source, targetPlace);

            if (!validateMove(game, move)) {
                // Move is invalid, skip
                continue;
            }

            // Check occupancy
            Piece pieceAtTarget = game.getBoard().getPieceAt(targetPlace);
            if (pieceAtTarget == null) {
                // Empty square
                if (!screenFound) {
                    // Can move freely if no screen has been found yet
                    moves.add(move);
                } else {
                    // Can't land on empty after a screen
                    // continue searching
                }
            } else {
                // Occupied square
                if (!screenFound) {
                    // First obstacle: mark screen found and continue
                    screenFound = true;
                } else {
                    // Second obstacle: check if opponent's piece
                    if (pieceAtTarget.getPlayer() != this.getPlayer()) {
                        // Capture move
                        moves.add(move);
                    }
                    // After encountering second obstacle, stop in this direction
                    break;
                }
            }
        }
    }

    return moves.toArray(new Move[0]);
}
```

**Note:** If `Place` has getter methods like `getRow()` and `getCol()`, replace `source.row` and `source.col` with `source.getRow()` and `source.getCol()`.

      Move move=new Move(source,targetPlace);
      if (!validateMove(game,move)) {
        continue;
      }
      Piece pieceAtTarget=game.getPieceAt(targetPlace);
      if (pieceAtTarget == null) {
        if (!screenFound) {
          moves.add(move);
        }
      }

        if (!screenFound) {
          screenFound=true;
        }
 else {
          if (pieceAtTarget.getPlayer() != this.getPlayer()) {
            moves.add(move);
          }
          break;
        }
      }
    }
  }
  return moves.toArray(new Move[0]);
}

@Override
public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Game game, Place source) {
    ArrayList<Move> moves = new ArrayList<>();
    int[][] directions = { {1, 0}, {-1, 0}, {0, 1}, {0, -1} }; // down, up, right, left
    int maxRow = game.getNumRows();
    int maxCol = game.getNumCols();

    for (int[] dir : directions) {
        int row = source.row;
        int col = source.col;
        boolean screenFound = false;

        while (true) {
            row += dir[0];
            col += dir[1];

            // Check boundary
            if (row < 0 || row >= maxRow || col < 0 || col >= maxCol) {
                break;
            }

            Place targetPlace = new Place(row, col);
            Move move = new Move(source, targetPlace);

            if (!validateMove(game, move)) {
                // Move is invalid, skip
                continue;
            }

            // Check occupancy
            Piece pieceAtTarget = game.getPieceAt(targetPlace);
            if (pieceAtTarget == null) {
                // Empty square
                if (!screenFound) {
                    // Can move freely if no screen has been found yet
                    moves.add(move);
                }
            } else {
                // Occupied square
                if (!screenFound) {
                    // First obstacle: mark screen found and continue
                    screenFound = true;
                } else {
                    // Second obstacle: check if opponent's piece
                    if (pieceAtTarget.getPlayer() != this.getPlayer()) {
                        // Capture move
                        moves.add(move);
                    }
                    // After encountering second obstacle, stop in this direction
                    break;
                }
            }
        }
    }

    return moves.toArray(new Move[0]);

public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {

Response Text:---
The `validate` method should check whether the move for an Archer piece is valid according to its movement rules, which are similar to the cannon in Chinese chess. Specifically, the Archer can move any number of empty squares along a rank or file, but capturing requires jumping over exactly one piece (the "screen") to capture an opponent's piece.

Here's a brief explanation of the logic:
- If the move is a simple move (not capturing), ensure there are no pieces in the path.
- If the move is a capture, ensure there is exactly one piece between the source and target, and the target contains an opponent's piece.

Below is a complete implementation of the `validate` method:

```java
@Override
public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
    if (!(game.getPiece(move.getSource()) instanceof Archer)) {
        return true;
    }

    int srcRow = move.getSource().getRow();
    int srcCol = move.getSource().getCol();
    int destRow = move.getDestination().getRow();
    int destCol = move.getDestination().getCol();

    // Check if move is along the same row or column
    if (srcRow != destRow && srcCol != destCol) {
        return false; // Invalid move: not straight line
    }

    int countPiecesBetween = 0;

    if (srcRow == destRow) {
        // Horizontal move
        int start = Math.min(srcCol, destCol) + 1;
        int end = Math.max(srcCol, destCol);
        for (int col = start; col < end; col++) {
            if (game.getPiece(move.getSource().withCol(col)) != null) {
                countPiecesBetween++;
            }
        }
    } else {
        // Vertical move
        int start = Math.min(srcRow, destRow) + 1;
        int end = Math.max(srcRow, destRow);
        for (int row = start; row < end; row++) {
            if (game.getPiece(move.getSource().withRow(row)) != null) {
                countPiecesBetween++;
            }
        }
    }

    boolean isCapture = game.getPiece(move.getDestination()) != null;
    if (isCapture) {
        // To capture, exactly one piece must be between source and destination
        return countPiecesBetween == 1;
    } else {
        // To move without capturing, path must be clear
        return countPiecesBetween == 0;
    }
}
```

**Note:** This implementation assumes that `move.getSource()` and `move.getDestination()` return objects with `getRow()` and `getCol()` methods, and that `game.getPiece()` returns `null` if the square is empty. Adjust accordingly if your actual classes differ.

To fix this, you should use the `getX()` and `getY()` methods (assuming `Place` uses these for coordinates), and create new `Place` instances with the desired coordinates directly, since `withRow()` and `withCol()` are not available.

Here's the corrected method:

```java
@Override
public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
    if (!(game.getPiece(move.getSource()) instanceof Archer)) {
        return true;
    }

    int srcX = move.getSource().getX();
    int srcY = move.getSource().getY();
    int destX = move.getDestination().getX();
    int destY = move.getDestination().getY();

    // Check if move is along the same row or column
    if (srcX != destX && srcY != destY) {
        return false; // Invalid move: not straight line
    }

    int countPiecesBetween = 0;

    if (srcX == destX) {
        // Vertical move
        int startY = Math.min(srcY, destY) + 1;
        int endY = Math.max(srcY, destY);
        for (int y = startY; y < endY; y++) {
            if (game.getPiece(new Place(srcX, y)) != null) {
                countPiecesBetween++;
            }
        }
    } else {
        // Horizontal move
        int startX = Math.min(srcX, destX) + 1;
        int endX = Math.max(srcX, destX);
        for (int x = startX; x < endX; x++) {
            if (game.getPiece(new Place(x, srcY)) != null) {
                countPiecesBetween++;
            }
        }
    }

    boolean isCapture = game.getPiece(move.getDestination()) != null;
    if (isCapture) {
        // To capture, exactly one piece must be between source and destination
        return countPiecesBetween == 1;
    } else {
        // To move without capturing, path must be clear
        return countPiecesBetween == 0;
    }
}

public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
    if (!(game.getPiece(move.getSource()) instanceof Archer)) {
        return true;

    int srcX = move.getSource().getX();
    int srcY = move.getSource().getY();
    int destX = move.getDestination().getX();
    int destY = move.getDestination().getY();

    // Check if move is along the same row or column
    if (srcX != destX && srcY != destY) {
        return false; // Invalid move: not straight line
    }

    int countPiecesBetween = 0;

    if (srcX == destX) {
        // Vertical move
        int startY = Math.min(srcY, destY) + 1;
        int endY = Math.max(srcY, destY);
        for (int y = startY; y < endY; y++) {
            if (game.getPiece(new Place(srcX, y)) != null) {
                countPiecesBetween++;
            }
        }
    } else {
        // Horizontal move
        int startX = Math.min(srcX, destX) + 1;
        int endX = Math.max(srcX, destX);
        for (int x = startX; x < endX; x++) {
            if (game.getPiece(new Place(x, srcY)) != null) {
                countPiecesBetween++;
            }
        }
    }

    boolean isCapture = game.getPiece(move.getDestination()) != null;
    if (isCapture) {
        // To capture, exactly one piece must be between source and destination
        return countPiecesBetween == 1;
    } else {
        // To move without capturing, path must be clear
        return countPiecesBetween == 0;
    }

The `validate` method is intended to check whether a move involving a Knight piece in chess is valid according to specific rules. Since the method currently returns `false` for Knight moves, the implementation should verify if the move is a valid Knight move based on its source and destination positions.

A valid Knight move in chess moves in an "L" shape: two squares in one direction and one square perpendicular to that. This can be checked by calculating the difference in row and column between the source and destination positions.

Here's a complete implementation of the `validate` method:

```java
@Override
public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
    if (!(game.getPiece(move.getSource()) instanceof Knight)) {
        return true;
    }
    int sourceRow = move.getSource().getRow();
    int sourceCol = move.getSource().getCol();
    int destRow = move.getDestination().getRow();
    int destCol = move.getDestination().getCol();

    int rowDiff = Math.abs(destRow - sourceRow);
    int colDiff = Math.abs(destCol - sourceCol);

    // Knight moves in an "L" shape: (2,1) or (1,2)
    boolean isValidKnightMove = (rowDiff == 2 && colDiff == 1) || (rowDiff == 1 && colDiff == 2);

    // Additional check: ensure destination is either empty or occupied by opponent's piece
    // (assuming game.getPiece returns null if empty)
    var destinationPiece = game.getPiece(move.getDestination());
    if (destinationPiece != null && destinationPiece.getColor() == game.getPiece(move.getSource()).getColor()) {
        return false; // Can't capture own piece
    }

    return isValidKnightMove;
}
```

- Checks if the piece at the source is a Knight.
- Calculates the row and column differences between source and destination.
- Validates if the move matches the Knight's "L" shape movement.
- Ensures the destination is either empty or occupied by an opponent's piece.
- Returns `true` if the move is valid; otherwise, `false`.

This implementation ensures the move adheres to the standard Knight movement rules in chess.

Response Text:---
The blocking rule for a Knight in Chinese chess (Xiangqi) states that the Knight's movement can be blocked if the "leg" position (the square adjacent to the source in the direction of movement) is occupied. To implement this, we need to determine the "leg" position based on the move's source and destination, then check if that position is occupied by any piece.

Here's the complete implementation of the `validate` method:

```java
@Override
public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
    if (!(game.getPiece(move.getSource()) instanceof Knight)) {
        return true;
    }

    int sourceRow = move.getSource().getRow();
    int sourceCol = move.getSource().getCol();
    int destRow = move.getDestination().getRow();
    int destCol = move.getDestination().getCol();

    int deltaRow = destRow - sourceRow;
    int deltaCol = destCol - sourceCol;

    // Determine the "leg" position based on move direction
    if (Math.abs(deltaRow) == 2 && Math.abs(deltaCol) == 1) {
        // Moving vertically two steps, leg is one step in the row direction
        int legRow = sourceRow + (deltaRow / 2);
        int legCol = sourceCol;
        if (game.getPiece(new Place(legRow, legCol)) != null) {
            return false; // blocked
        }
    } else if (Math.abs(deltaRow) == 1 && Math.abs(deltaCol) == 2) {
        // Moving horizontally two steps, leg is one step in the column direction
        int legRow = sourceRow;
        int legCol = sourceCol + (deltaCol / 2);
        if (game.getPiece(new Place(legRow, legCol)) != null) {
            return false; // blocked
        }
    }
    return true; // not blocked
}
```

**Explanation:**
- Checks if the piece at the source is a Knight.
- Calculates the move's delta in rows and columns.
- Determines the "leg" position based on the move's direction.
- Checks if the "leg" position is occupied; if so, the move is invalid (blocked).
- Returns `true` if the move is valid (not blocked), otherwise `false`.

This implementation correctly enforces the blocking rule for Knights in Chinese chess.

The task is to implement the `nextMove` method for the `ConsolePlayer` class. This method should prompt the user for input, validate the input format, ensure the move is among the available moves, and return a valid `Move` object. The implementation involves reading user input, parsing it, validating the move, and handling invalid inputs gracefully by prompting again until a valid move is entered.

Here's a complete implementation:

```java
@Override
public Move nextMove(Game game, Move[] availableMoves) {
    Scanner scanner = new Scanner(System.in);
    Move chosenMove = null;

    while (true) {
        System.out.println("Enter your move (e.g., a1->b3):");
        String input = scanner.nextLine().trim();

        // Parse the move from input
        Move move = parseMove(input);
        if (move == null) {
            System.out.println("Invalid format. Please enter move in format 'a1->b3'.");
            continue;
        }

        // Validate the move against available moves
        boolean isValid = false;
        for (Move m : availableMoves) {
            if (m.equals(move)) {
                isValid = true;
                chosenMove = m;
                break;
            }
        }

        if (!isValid) {
            System.out.println("Invalid move. Please select a move from the available options.");
            continue;
        }

        // Optional: Additional validation if needed
        String validationError = validateMove(game, chosenMove);
        if (validationError != null) {
            System.out.println("Invalid move: " + validationError);
            continue;
        }

        // If all checks pass, break the loop
        break;
    }

    return chosenMove;
}

package assignment.player;

import assignment.protocol.Game;
import assignment.piece.*;
import assignment.protocol.Color;
import assignment.protocol.Move;
import assignment.protocol.Place;
import assignment.protocol.Player;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;

import java.util.Scanner;

/**
 * The player that makes move according to user input from console.
 */
public class ConsolePlayer extends Player {
	public ConsolePlayer(String name, Color color) {
		super(name, color);
	}

	public ConsolePlayer(String name) {
		this(name, Color.GREEN);
	}

	/**
	 * Choose a move from available moves.
	 * This method will be called by {@link Game} object to get the move that the player wants to make when it is the
	 * player's turn.
	 * <p>
	 * {@link ConsolePlayer} returns a move according to user's input in the console.
	 * The console input format should conform the format described in the assignment description.
	 * (e.g. {@literal a1->b3} means move the {@link Piece} at {@link Place}(x=0,y=0) to {@link Place}(x=1,y=2))
	 * Note that in the {@link Game}.board, the index starts from 0 in both x and y dimension, while in the console
	 * display, x dimension index starts from 'a' and y dimension index starts from 1.
	 * <p>
	 * Hint: be sure to handle invalid input to avoid invalid {@link Move}s.
	 * <p>
	 * <strong>Attention: Student should make sure the {@link Move} returned is valid.</strong>
	 * <p>
	 * <strong>Attention: {@link Place} object uses integer as index of x and y-axis, both starting from 0 to
	 * facilitate programming.
	 * This is VERY different from the coordinate used in console display.</strong>
	 *
	 * @param game           the current game object
	 * @param availableMoves available moves for this player to choose from.
	 * @return the chosen move
	 */
	@Override
	public Move nextMove(Game game, Move[] availableMoves) {
		// TODO student implementation
		return availableMoves[0];
	}

	private String validateMove(Game game, Move move) {
		var rules = new Rule[] { new OutOfBoundaryRule(), new OccupiedRule(), new VacantRule(), new NilMoveRule(),
				new FirstNMovesProtectionRule(game.getConfiguration().getNumMovesProtection()), new ArcherMoveRule(),
				new KnightMoveRule(), new KnightBlockRule(), };
		for (var rule : rules) {
			if (!rule.validate(game, move)) {
				return rule.getDescription();
			}

			var piece = game.getPiece(move.getSource());
			if (piece == null) {
				return "No piece at " + move.getSource().toString();
			}
			if (!this.equals(piece.getPlayer())) {
				return "Cannot move a piece not belonging to you";
			}
		}
		return null;
	}

	private static Place parsePlace(String str) {
		if (str.length() < 2) {
			return null;
		}
		try {
			var x = str.charAt(0) - 'a';
			var y = Integer.parseInt(str.substring(1)) - 1;
			return new Place(x, y);
		} catch (NumberFormatException e) {
			return null;
		}
	}

	private static Move parseMove(String str) {
		var segments = str.split("->");
		if (segments.length < 2) {
			return null;
		}
		var source = parsePlace(segments[0].strip());
		if (source == null) {
			return null;
		}
		var destination = parsePlace(segments[1].strip());
		if (destination == null) {
			return null;
		}
		return new Move(source, destination);
	}
}

	 * Moves the player in the given direction.

	 * before this method was called.
	 * </p>
	 *
	 * @param direction Direction to move the player in.
	 * @return An instance of {@link MoveResult} representing the result of this action.

	public MoveResult makeMove(final Direction direction) {

		return null;

	 * Undoes a move by reverting all changes performed by the specified move.
	 *
	 * <p>

	 * </p>
	 *
	 * @param prevMove The {@link MoveResult} object to revert.
	 */
	public void undoMove(final MoveResult prevMove) {
		// TODO
	}

	/**
	 * Tries to move the player from a position in the specified direction as far as possible.
	 *
	 * <p>
	 * Note that this method does <b>NOT</b> actually move the player. It just tries to move the player and return
	 * the state of the player as-if it has been moved.
	 * </p>
	 *
	 * @param position  The original position of the player.
	 * @param direction The direction to move the player in.
	 * @return An instance of {@link MoveResult} representing the type of the move and the position of the player after
	 * moving.
	 */
	@NotNull
	private MoveResult tryMove(@NotNull final Position position, @NotNull final Direction direction) {
		Objects.requireNonNull(position);
		Objects.requireNonNull(direction);

		final var collectedGems = new ArrayList<Position>();
		final var collectedExtraLives = new ArrayList<Position>();
		Position lastValidPosition = position;
		do {
			final Position newPosition = offsetPosition(lastValidPosition, direction);
			if (newPosition == null) {
				break;
			}

			lastValidPosition = newPosition;

			if (gameBoard.getCell(newPosition) instanceof StopCell) {
				break;
			}

			if (gameBoard.getCell(newPosition) instanceof EntityCell entityCell) {
				if (entityCell.getEntity() instanceof Mine) {
					return new MoveResult.Valid.Dead(position, newPosition);
				}

				if (entityCell.getEntity() instanceof Gem) {
					collectedGems.add(newPosition);
				} else if (entityCell.getEntity() instanceof ExtraLife) {
					collectedExtraLives.add(newPosition);
				}
			}
		} while (true);

		if (lastValidPosition.equals(position)) {
			return new MoveResult.Invalid(position);
		}

		return new MoveResult.Valid.Alive(lastValidPosition, position, collectedGems, collectedExtraLives);
	}

	/**
	 * Offsets the {@link Position} in the specified {@link Direction} by one step.
	 *
	 * @param position  The original position.
	 * @param direction The direction to offset.
	 * @return The given position offset by one in the specified direction. If the new position is outside of the game
	 * board, or contains a non-{@link EntityCell}, returns {@code null}.
	 */
	@Nullable
	private Position offsetPosition(@NotNull final Position position, @NotNull final Direction direction) {
		Objects.requireNonNull(position);
		Objects.requireNonNull(direction);

		final var newPos = position.offsetByOrNull(direction.getOffset(), gameBoard.getNumRows(),
				gameBoard.getNumCols());

		if (newPos == null) {
			return null;
		}
		if (!(gameBoard.getCell(newPos) instanceof EntityCell)) {
			return null;
		}

		return newPos;
	}
}

public MoveResult makeMove(final Direction direction) {

    // Attempt to move the player in the specified direction

        if (validResult instanceof MoveResult.Valid.Dead) {
            // Player died, do not mutate the game board
            return validResult;

            // Save current state to revert if needed
            // Save the current state before mutation for undo
            // (Assuming there's a way to store previous state, or we can proceed)
            // Mutate the game board: move player, remove collected gems/lives, handle death if any

            // Place player at new position
            gameBoard.setCell(aliveResult.getNewPosition(), new PlayerCell());
            // Remove collected gems
            for (Position gemPos : aliveResult.getCollectedGems()) {
                gameBoard.setCell(gemPos, new EmptyCell());
            }
            // Remove collected extra lives
            for (Position lifePos : aliveResult.getCollectedExtraLives()) {
                gameBoard.setCell(lifePos, new EmptyCell());

            gameBoard.setPlayerPosition(aliveResult.getNewPosition());
            return aliveResult;
        }
    }

    return moveResult;
}

public void undoMove(final MoveResult prevMove) {
    if (prevMove == null) {
        return;
    }

    if (prevMove instanceof MoveResult.Valid validMove) {
        Position originalPosition = validMove.getOriginalPosition();
        Position newPosition = validMove.getNewPosition();

        // Move player back to original position
        gameBoard.setCell(newPosition, gameBoard.getCell(newPosition).withEmpty());
        gameBoard.setCell(originalPosition, new PlayerCell());
        gameBoard.setPlayerPosition(originalPosition);

        // Restore collected gems
        for (Position gemPos : validMove.getCollectedGems()) {
            gameBoard.setCell(gemPos, new Gem());
        }

        // Restore collected extra lives
        for (Position lifePos : validMove.getCollectedExtraLives()) {
            gameBoard.setCell(lifePos, new ExtraLife());
        }

        // If the move resulted in death, no additional action needed as we've reverted to previous state
        // If needed, handle other states or effects here
    } else if (prevMove instanceof MoveResult.Invalid) {
        // No changes to revert if move was invalid
        // Possibly reset player position if needed
    } else if (prevMove instanceof MoveResult.Valid.Dead deadMove) {
        Position originalPosition = deadMove.getOriginalPosition();
        Position deadPosition = deadMove.getNewPosition();

        // Remove the dead cell (if needed) and restore player to original position
        gameBoard.setCell(deadPosition, gameBoard.getCell(deadPosition).withEmpty());
        gameBoard.setCell(originalPosition, new PlayerCell());
        gameBoard.setPlayerPosition(originalPosition);

    }

	 * Hint: Undoing a move is effectively the same as reversing everything you have done to make a move.
	 * </p>
	 *
	 * @param prevMove The {@link MoveResult} object to revert.
	 */
	public void undoMove(final MoveResult prevMove) {
		// TODO
	}

	/**
	 * Tries to move the player from a position in the specified direction as far as possible.
	 *
	 * <p>
	 * Note that this method does <b>NOT</b> actually move the player. It just tries to move the player and return
	 * the state of the player as-if it has been moved.
	 * </p>
	 *
	 * @param position  The original position of the player.
	 * @param direction The direction to move the player in.
	 * @return An instance of {@link MoveResult} representing the type of the move and the position of the player after
	 * moving.
	 */
	@NotNull
	private MoveResult tryMove(@NotNull final Position position, @NotNull final Direction direction) {
		Objects.requireNonNull(position);
		Objects.requireNonNull(direction);

		final var collectedGems = new ArrayList<Position>();
		final var collectedExtraLives = new ArrayList<Position>();
		Position lastValidPosition = position;
		do {
			final Position newPosition = offsetPosition(lastValidPosition, direction);
			if (newPosition == null) {
				break;
			}

			lastValidPosition = newPosition;

			if (gameBoard.getCell(newPosition) instanceof StopCell) {
				break;
			}

			if (gameBoard.getCell(newPosition) instanceof EntityCell entityCell) {
				if (entityCell.getEntity() instanceof Mine) {
					return new MoveResult.Valid.Dead(position, newPosition);
				}

				if (entityCell.getEntity() instanceof Gem) {
					collectedGems.add(newPosition);
				} else if (entityCell.getEntity() instanceof ExtraLife) {
					collectedExtraLives.add(newPosition);
				}
			}
		} while (true);

		if (lastValidPosition.equals(position)) {
			return new MoveResult.Invalid(position);
		}

		return new MoveResult.Valid.Alive(lastValidPosition, position, collectedGems, collectedExtraLives);
	}

	/**
	 * Offsets the {@link Position} in the specified {@link Direction} by one step.
	 *
	 * @param position  The original position.
	 * @param direction The direction to offset.
	 * @return The given position offset by one in the specified direction. If the new position is outside of the game
	 * board, or contains a non-{@link EntityCell}, returns {@code null}.
	 */
	@Nullable
	private Position offsetPosition(@NotNull final Position position, @NotNull final Direction direction) {
		Objects.requireNonNull(position);
		Objects.requireNonNull(direction);

		final var newPos = position.offsetByOrNull(direction.getOffset(), gameBoard.getNumRows(),
				gameBoard.getNumCols());

		if (newPos == null) {
			return null;
		}
		if (!(gameBoard.getCell(newPos) instanceof EntityCell)) {
			return null;
		}

		return newPos;
	}

	public void GameBoardController(final GameBoard gameBoard) {
		this.gameBoard = Objects.requireNonNull(gameBoard, "gameBoard must not be null");
	}

	public MoveResult makeMove(final Direction direction) {
		Position currentPosition = gameBoard.getPlayerPosition();
		MoveResult moveResult = tryMove(currentPosition, direction);
		if (moveResult instanceof MoveResult.Valid validResult) {
			if (validResult instanceof MoveResult.Valid.Dead) {
				return validResult;
			} else if (validResult instanceof MoveResult.Valid.Alive aliveResult) {
				gameBoard.setCell(currentPosition, gameBoard.getCell(currentPosition).withEmpty());
				gameBoard.setCell(aliveResult.getNewPosition(), new PlayerCell());
				for (Position gemPos : aliveResult.getCollectedGems()) {
					gameBoard.setCell(gemPos, new EmptyCell());
				}
				for (Position lifePos : aliveResult.getCollectedExtraLives()) {
					gameBoard.setCell(lifePos, new EmptyCell());
				}
				gameBoard.setPlayerPosition(aliveResult.getNewPosition());
				return aliveResult;
			}
		}
		return moveResult;
	}
}

```java
package pa1.model;

import org.jetbrains.annotations.Nullable;

/**
 * An entity on the game board.
 */
public abstract class Entity implements BoardElement {

    @Nullable
    private EntityCell owner;

    /**
     * Default constructor initializing owner to null.
     */
    public Entity() {
        this.owner = null;
    }

    /**

     */

        this.owner = owner;
    }

    /**
     * @return The {@link EntityCell} owning this entity, or {@code null} if this entity is not bound to a cell.
     */
    public final EntityCell getOwner() {
        return this.owner;
    }

    protected void Entity() {
        this.owner = null;
    }

    protected void Entity(final EntityCell owner) {
        this.owner = owner;
    }

    public final EntityCell setOwner(final EntityCell owner) {
        EntityCell previousOwner = this.owner;
        this.owner = owner;
        return previousOwner;
    }
}

The `setEntity` method needs to perform ownership transfer logic: it should unset the owner of the previous entity, clear the previous entity's cell reference, set the owner of the new entity to this cell, and update the cell's entity reference. Here's a complete implementation:

```java
public Entity setEntity(final Entity newEntity) {
    // Store the current entity to return later
    Entity previousEntity = this.entity;

    // If there is a current entity, unset its owner and cell reference
    if (this.entity != null) {
        this.entity.setOwner(null);
        this.entity.setCell(null);
    }

    // If the new entity is not null, set its owner to this cell and update its cell reference
    if (newEntity != null) {
        // Unset the previous cell owning the new entity, if any
        EntityCell previousOwnerCell = newEntity.getOwner();
        if (previousOwnerCell != null && previousOwnerCell.getEntity() == newEntity) {
            previousOwnerCell.entity = null;
        }
        newEntity.setOwner(this);
        newEntity.setCell(this);
    }

    // Set the new entity in this cell
    this.entity = newEntity;

    // Return the previous entity
    return previousEntity;
}
```

**Note:** This implementation assumes that the `Entity` class has `setOwner(EntityCell owner)` and `setCell(EntityCell cell)` methods, and that `getOwner()` returns the current owner cell. If such methods are named differently, adjust accordingly.

public Entity setEntity(final Entity newEntity) {
    // Store the current entity to return later
    Entity previousEntity = this.entity;

    // If there is a current entity, unset its owner and cell reference
    if (this.entity != null) {
        this.entity.setOwner(null);
        this.entity.setCell(null);
    }

    // If the new entity is not null, set its owner to this cell and update its cell reference
    if (newEntity != null) {
        // Unset the previous cell owning the new entity, if any
        EntityCell previousOwnerCell = newEntity.getOwner();
        if (previousOwnerCell != null && previousOwnerCell.getEntity() == newEntity) {
            previousOwnerCell.entity = null;
        }
        newEntity.setOwner(this);
        newEntity.setCell(this);
    }

    // Set the new entity in this cell
    this.entity = newEntity;

    // Return the previous entity
    return previousEntity;

package pa1.model;

import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.Nullable;

/**
 * A {@link Cell} on the game board which can contain an {@link Entity}.
 *
 * <p>
 * This class should observe and enforce the following constraints:
 * </p>
 * <ul>
 *     <li>There must be at most one entity owned by each cell; In other words, there should never be two entities'
 *     {@link Entity#getOwner()} pointing to the same {@link EntityCell}.</li>
 *     <li>There must be at most one cell owning each entity; In other words, there should never be two cells'
 *     {@link EntityCell#getEntity()} pointing to the same {@link Entity}.</li>
 * </ul>
 * <p>
 * More information is provided in the Javadoc of the methods in this class.
 * </p>
 */
public class EntityCell extends Cell {

	/**
	 * The entity which resides on this cell.
	 */
	@Nullable
	Entity entity = null;

	/**
	 * @return The entity currently present in this cell, or {@code null} if there is no entity present.
	 */
	public final Entity getEntity() {
		// TODO
		return null;
	}

	@Override
	public char toUnicodeChar() {
		return getEntity() != null ? getEntity().toUnicodeChar() : '.';
	}

	@Override
	public char toASCIIChar() {
		return getEntity() != null ? getEntity().toASCIIChar() : '.';
	}

	public void EntityCell(final Position position) {
		super(position);
	}

	public void EntityCell(final Position position, final Entity initialEntity) {
		super(position);
		if (initialEntity != null) {
			initialEntity.setOwner(this);
			this.entity = initialEntity;
		}
	}

	public Entity setEntity(final Entity newEntity) {
		Entity previousEntity = this.entity;
		if (this.entity != null) {
			this.entity.setOwner(null);
			this.entity.setCell(null);
		}
		if (newEntity != null) {
			EntityCell previousOwnerCell = newEntity.getOwner();
			if (previousOwnerCell != null && previousOwnerCell.getEntity() == newEntity) {
				previousOwnerCell.entity = null;
			}
			newEntity.setOwner(this);
			newEntity.setCell(this);
		}
		this.entity = newEntity;
		return previousEntity;
	}
}

To fix the errors, you should add appropriate constructors to EntityCell that accept a Position and optionally an Entity, enabling instantiation as shown in the tests.

package pa1.model;

import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.Nullable;

/**
 * A {@link Cell} on the game board which can contain an {@link Entity}.
 *
 * <p>
 * This class should observe and enforce the following constraints:
 * </p>
 * <ul>
 *     <li>There must be at most one entity owned by each cell; In other words, there should never be two entities'
 *     {@link Entity#getOwner()} pointing to the same {@link EntityCell}.</li>
 *     <li>There must be at most one cell owning each entity; In other words, there should never be two cells'
 *     {@link EntityCell#getEntity()} pointing to the same {@link Entity}.</li>
 * </ul>
 * <p>
 * More information is provided in the Javadoc of the methods in this class.
 * </p>
 */
public class EntityCell extends Cell {

	/**
	 * The entity which resides on this cell.
	 */
	@Nullable
	Entity entity = null;

	/**
	 * @return The entity currently present in this cell, or {@code null} if there is no entity present.
	 */
	public final Entity getEntity() {
		// TODO
		return null;
	}

	@Override
	public char toUnicodeChar() {
		return getEntity() != null ? getEntity().toUnicodeChar() : '.';
	}

	@Override
	public char toASCIIChar() {
		return getEntity() != null ? getEntity().toASCIIChar() : '.';
	}

	public void EntityCell(final Position position) {
		super(position);
	}

	public void EntityCell(final Position position, final Entity initialEntity) {
		super(position);
		if (initialEntity != null) {
			initialEntity.setOwner(this);
			this.entity = initialEntity;
		}
	}

	public Entity setEntity(final Entity newEntity) {
		Entity previousEntity = this.entity;
		if (this.entity != null) {
			this.entity.setOwner(null);
			this.entity.setCell(null);
		}
		if (newEntity != null) {
			EntityCell previousOwnerCell = newEntity.getOwner();
			if (previousOwnerCell != null && previousOwnerCell.getEntity() == newEntity) {
				previousOwnerCell.entity = null;
			}
			newEntity.setOwner(this);
			newEntity.setCell(this);
		}
		this.entity = newEntity;
		return previousEntity;
	}
}

To fix these errors, you should define such constructors in the `EntityCell` class, ensuring they accept a `Position` and an `Entity` (or specific subclasses like `Player`, `Mine`, `Gem`, etc.) and properly initialize the object.

**Brief explanation:**  
The existing `EntityCell` class only has a constructor accepting only `Position` or default constructor. The tests and serializer expect constructors that accept both `Position` and an `Entity` (or specific subclasses). Adding these constructors will resolve the compilation errors related to object creation with entities.

**Correct Java class code (add these constructors to `EntityCell`):**

```java
public class EntityCell extends Cell {
    @Nullable
    Entity entity = null;

    public EntityCell(@NotNull Position position, @Nullable Entity entity) {
        super(position);
        this.entity = entity;
        if (entity != null) {
            entity.setCell(this);
        }
    }

    public EntityCell(@NotNull Position position) {
        this(position, null);
    }
}
```

**Note:**  
- Ensure that `Entity` and its subclasses (`Player`, `Mine`, `Gem`, etc.) have the `setCell(EntityCell)` method implemented, as the constructor calls `entity.setCell(this)`.  
- Also, verify that your `Cell` class has a constructor accepting `Position`.  
- This will allow creating `EntityCell` instances with both position and entity, matching the expected usage in tests and serialization.
